Both did land on exactly one result — Inclusive Components — so the pieces I asked for are all there: I can require an exact phrase, narrow to a label, and knock out a site I don't want, all in one search. Good.

Between the two, for everyday use I prefer the **guided-controls version**. Typing `label:Design "keyboard navigation" -site:css-tricks.com` is powerful, but I'd have to remember the special words and punctuation — "label:", the minus, "site:" — and I'd get it wrong half the time. The guided one lets me just type what I remember and pick the label and the site-to-exclude from clear controls, without memorizing any syntax. That's much more my speed. (No objection to the typed version existing for people who like it, but the guided one is what I'd reach for.)

One thing I noticed while trying them, and it's part of this same combined-search idea: both versions treat every condition as something that *must* match — it's always "this AND that AND not that." Sometimes what I actually want is an *either/or*: "show me anything tagged Design **or** tagged Reference," where matching just one is enough. I don't see a way to say "or" in either version. Could we add an either/or option so I can gather things that match one condition or another, not only ones that satisfy all of them at once?
